title: THE TENT OF MEETING AT SHILOH

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The whole assembly of the Israelites gathered at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there. The country was brought under their control, but there were still seven tribes who had not yet received their inheritance - Josh 18:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The whole nation gathers at Shiloh, and there they set up the tent of meeting — the place where God's presence dwelt among them. It is a significant moment. Before the remaining land is distributed, before any more business is done, God's dwelling place is established at the centre of the people. Worship comes first; the presence of God is put at the heart of the community.

There is wisdom in this order. Israel could easily have rushed straight into dividing the leftover land, eager to settle their claims. Instead, the tent of meeting is set up first. God's presence among His people takes priority over the practical matters, however important those matters are. The centre of the nation was to be the place where God met with them.

This speaks to how we order our own lives. It is tempting to rush into the business of living — the tasks, the plans, the unfinished matters — and fit God in around the edges. But Shiloh reminds us to put God's presence at the centre first. When we seek Him first, everything else finds its proper place (Matt 6:33). Under the new covenant, we no longer go to a tent; through Christ we ourselves have become the dwelling place of God's Spirit (1 Cor 3:16). Let His presence be the centre, and the rest of life will order itself around Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you put God's presence at the centre, or fit Him around the edges?
- What would it look like to seek God first before rushing into your tasks?
- How does it change things to know God's Spirit now dwells within you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to put Your presence at the centre of my life rather than the edges. Teach me to seek You first, and to live as the dwelling place of Your Spirit in Christ. Amen.
